tasks.title: The KVM API version
tasks.statement: This is the roadmap exercise: a tiny program that opens /dev/kvm and asks for the API version. Write int kvm_api_version(void): open /dev/kvm with O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC, call ioctl(fd, KVM_GET_API_VERSION, 0), close the descriptor and return the version. If open or ioctl fails, return -errno (the negated error number; save errno before close, because close may overwrite it). The descriptor must not leak on any path. The sandbox has no /dev/kvm: the driver plugs in a MODEL of the kernel (a lab simplification; the constants and structures are the real ones from linux/kvm.h, the model's behaviour is described in the statement). Write ordinary code with open, ioctl, close, mmap, as for the real device.
tasks.hint: The version is the return value of ioctl, not data through a pointer. On a real kernel it is 12.

tasks.title: Open /dev/kvm with a version check
tasks.statement: A program that works with KVM must refuse to run if the API version is not KVM_API_VERSION (12). Write int kvm_open(void): open /dev/kvm (O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC), check the version and return the open descriptor. If open fails, return -errno. If ioctl fails, return the -errno of that call. If the version is not 12, return -EPROTO. On any error the descriptor must be closed. The sandbox has no /dev/kvm: the driver plugs in a MODEL of the kernel (a lab simplification; the constants and structures are the real ones from linux/kvm.h, the model's behaviour is described in the statement). Write ordinary code with open, ioctl, close, mmap, as for the real device.
tasks.hint: Compare with the KVM_API_VERSION constant from the header, not a number in your code. Close the descriptor before return, but after you saved errno.

tasks.title: KVM extensions
tasks.statement: Before using a feature, a VMM asks the kernel with ioctl(kvm, KVM_CHECK_EXTENSION, cap): 0 means unsupported, a positive number means supported (sometimes the number carries data, such as how many vCPUs are allowed). Write two functions. int kvm_cap_value(int kvm, int cap): return the result of the call, or -errno on error. int kvm_missing(int kvm, const int *caps, int n, int *missing): store in missing (in order) the capabilities from caps that are unsupported and return how many there are; if any call fails, return -errno immediately. The sandbox has no /dev/kvm: the driver plugs in a MODEL of the kernel (a lab simplification; the constants and structures are the real ones from linux/kvm.h, the model's behaviour is described in the statement). Write ordinary code with open, ioctl, close, mmap, as for the real device.
tasks.hint: kvm_missing is easy to write on top of kvm_cap_value. An error is a negative value, while "unsupported" is exactly zero.

tasks.title: A VM and vCPUs: three levels of descriptors
tasks.statement: KVM has three levels of descriptors: the system one (/dev/kvm), the VM (given by KVM_CREATE_VM) and the vCPU (given by KVM_CREATE_VCPU issued on the VM descriptor). Write int vm_create(int kvm, int nvcpus, int *vcpu_fds): create the VM with ioctl(kvm, KVM_CREATE_VM, 0) and nvcpus virtual processors numbered 0, 1, ..., nvcpus-1 with ioctl(vm, KVM_CREATE_VCPU, number). Store the vCPU descriptors in vcpu_fds and return the VM descriptor. If something fails, close everything this function managed to open (the kvm descriptor is not yours, do not close it) and return -errno. In the model a VM has at most eight vCPUs (the ninth gives EINVAL), a repeated number gives EEXIST. A request of the wrong level (for example KVM_RUN on a VM descriptor) is rejected by the model with ENOTTY; a real kernel answers ENOTTY or EINVAL there, depending on the descriptor and the architecture. The sandbox has no /dev/kvm: the driver plugs in a MODEL of the kernel (a lab simplification; the constants and structures are the real ones from linux/kvm.h, the model's behaviour is described in the statement). Write ordinary code with open, ioctl, close, mmap, as for the real device.
tasks.hint: The vCPU number is the third argument of ioctl. When vCPU i fails, close the previous i of them and the VM itself, saving errno before close.

tasks.title: Guest memory: an ordinary mmap
tasks.statement: A guest's RAM in KVM is just memory of the VMM process: you allocate it with mmap and tell the kernel at which guest physical address it appears. Write int guest_mem(int vm, int slot, uint64_t gpa, size_t size, const void *image, size_t len, void **host): round size up to whole pages (sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE)); if len is larger than the rounded size, return -E2BIG without allocating anything; allocate anonymous private memory with mmap(NULL, size, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0), copy the image (len bytes) to its start, register it with ioctl(vm, KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION, &region) using a struct kvm_userspace_memory_region (slot, flags = 0, guest_phys_addr = gpa, memory_size, userspace_addr), store the address in *host and return 0. If mmap or ioctl fails, return -errno without leaving an extra mapping (munmap). The model repeats the kernel's checks: the guest address and the size are multiples of the page (else EINVAL), the slot number is below 32 (else EINVAL), slots must not overlap in guest addresses (EEXIST). The sandbox has no /dev/kvm: the driver plugs in a MODEL of the kernel (a lab simplification; the constants and structures are the real ones from linux/kvm.h, the model's behaviour is described in the statement). Write ordinary code with open, ioctl, close, mmap, as for the real device.
tasks.hint: userspace_addr is (uintptr_t)pointer, not a pointer. Save errno before munmap.

tasks.title: The KVM_RUN loop and a serial port
tasks.statement: The heart of every VMM is a loop: call KVM_RUN, decode the exit reason, handle it, repeat. Write int run_serial(int vcpu, struct kvm_run *run, char *out, size_t cap). The driver has already mapped struct kvm_run (the argument run, an mmap of the vCPU descriptor with the size from KVM_GET_VCPU_MMAP_SIZE). KVM_RUN returns 0 when the guest exited and the reason is in run->exit_reason; -1 with EINTR means "a signal interrupted, call again". Handle it like this: EINTR - call again; any other KVM_RUN error - return -errno; KVM_EXIT_IO with direction KVM_EXIT_IO_OUT on port 0x3f8 is a "serial port": append the size*count bytes at (char *)run + run->io.data_offset to out (out holds at most cap-1 characters, drop the extra ones but keep running the guest); ignore output to other ports; answer input (KVM_EXIT_IO_IN) from any port with 0xFF bytes (size*count bytes at the same data_offset); KVM_EXIT_HLT ends the work: put a NUL byte at the end of out and return the number of stored characters; any other exit - return -EIO. The model's guest is not real machine code but a toy program (a lab simplification) placed in guest memory from address 0. Commands: 0x00 halt (exit KVM_EXIT_HLT); 0x01 pL pH v output byte v to port pH:pL (KVM_EXIT_IO, direction OUT, size 1, count 1, the data is at run + data_offset); 0x02 pL pH input from a port (KVM_EXIT_IO, direction IN: put the answer at the same data_offset before the next KVM_RUN); 0x05 pL pH output the accumulator acc to a port; 0x06 v add v to acc; 0xFF KVM_EXIT_SHUTDOWN; an unknown code gives KVM_EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR. The sandbox has no /dev/kvm: the driver plugs in a MODEL of the kernel (a lab simplification; the constants and structures are the real ones from linux/kvm.h, the model's behaviour is described in the statement). Write ordinary code with open, ioctl, close, mmap, as for the real device.
tasks.hint: The loop is for (;;) { r = ioctl(vcpu, KVM_RUN, 0); ... }. The port data lives inside the run mapping, not in the io structure.

tasks.title: A device in guest addresses: KVM_EXIT_MMIO
tasks.statement: When the guest touches a guest physical address where there is no memory, KVM returns KVM_EXIT_MMIO, and the VMM plays the device itself. Write int run_device(int vcpu, struct kvm_run *run, char *out, size_t cap). The driver has already mapped struct kvm_run (the argument run, an mmap of the vCPU descriptor with the size from KVM_GET_VCPU_MMAP_SIZE). KVM_RUN returns 0 when the guest exited and the reason is in run->exit_reason; -1 with EINTR means "a signal interrupted, call again". As in the previous task: EINTR calls again, any other error gives -errno, output to port 0x3f8 (OUT, the byte at (char *)run + run->io.data_offset) is appended to out (at most cap-1 characters), other port output is ignored, KVM_EXIT_HLT ends the work (a NUL at the end of out, return the number of characters), any other exit apart from those described below gives -EIO. New: the KVM_EXIT_MMIO exit. The model has a counter device at address 0x10000000: a read (run->mmio.is_write == 0) returns the counter's current value (one byte, put it into run->mmio.data[0]) and increments the counter by one; a write (is_write == 1) sets the counter to run->mmio.data[0]. The counter is one byte and starts at zero. Answer a read at any other address with the byte 0xFF and ignore a write at another address. The access length is always one byte. The model's guest is not real machine code but a toy program (a lab simplification) placed in guest memory from address 0. Commands: 0x00 halt (exit KVM_EXIT_HLT); 0x01 pL pH v output byte v to port pH:pL (KVM_EXIT_IO, direction OUT, size 1, count 1, the data is at run + data_offset); 0x02 pL pH input from a port (KVM_EXIT_IO, direction IN: put the answer at the same data_offset before the next KVM_RUN); 0x05 pL pH output the accumulator acc to a port; 0x06 v add v to acc; 0xFF KVM_EXIT_SHUTDOWN; an unknown code gives KVM_EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR. Also: 0x03 a0 a1 a2 a3 v write byte v at address a3a2a1a0 (KVM_EXIT_MMIO, is_write 1); 0x04 a0 a1 a2 a3 read a byte from that address into acc (you provide the answer, in run->mmio.data[0], before the next KVM_RUN). The sandbox has no /dev/kvm: the driver plugs in a MODEL of the kernel (a lab simplification; the constants and structures are the real ones from linux/kvm.h, the model's behaviour is described in the statement). Write ordinary code with open, ioctl, close, mmap, as for the real device.
tasks.hint: Keep the device state (the counter) in a local variable of the function. For a read, fill data[0] before the next KVM_RUN.

tasks.title: The whole tiny guest
tasks.statement: Put it all together in one VMM, without libvirt or QEMU. Write int tiny_guest(const uint8_t *prog, size_t len, char *out, size_t cap): 1) open /dev/kvm (O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC) and check that the API version equals KVM_API_VERSION (else -EPROTO); 2) create a VM; 3) mmap one page (4096 bytes) of guest memory, copy prog into it and register it in slot 0 at guest address 0 (if len is larger than a page, return -E2BIG without allocating anything); 4) create vCPU number 0; 5) learn the size of the kvm_run area with ioctl(kvm, KVM_GET_VCPU_MMAP_SIZE, 0) and map it with mmap of the vCPU descriptor (PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED, offset 0); 6) run the KVM_RUN loop: EINTR calls again; output to port 0x3f8 (the byte at (char *)run + run->io.data_offset) is appended to out (at most cap-1 characters); ignore other I/O, answer input with 0xFF bytes; KVM_EXIT_HLT is success (a NUL at the end of out, the result is the number of characters); any other exit is -EIO; 7) on every path release everything you opened and mapped. If a call fails at some step, return its -errno. Remember: the kvm_run area is larger than one page, take the size from the kernel, not sizeof(struct kvm_run). The model's guest is not real machine code but a toy program (a lab simplification) placed in guest memory from address 0. Commands: 0x00 halt (exit KVM_EXIT_HLT); 0x01 pL pH v output byte v to port pH:pL (KVM_EXIT_IO, direction OUT, size 1, count 1, the data is at run + data_offset); 0x02 pL pH input from a port (KVM_EXIT_IO, direction IN: put the answer at the same data_offset before the next KVM_RUN); 0x05 pL pH output the accumulator acc to a port; 0x06 v add v to acc; 0xFF KVM_EXIT_SHUTDOWN; an unknown code gives KVM_EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR. The sandbox has no /dev/kvm: the driver plugs in a MODEL of the kernel (a lab simplification; the constants and structures are the real ones from linux/kvm.h, the model's behaviour is described in the statement). Write ordinary code with open, ioctl, close, mmap, as for the real device.
tasks.hint: A chain of steps with cleanup labels (goto) or a helper run_loop is convenient. Release the kvm_run mapping with munmap and close the three descriptors.

tasks.title: Who can open /dev/kvm
tasks.statement: open("/dev/kvm", O_RDWR) can fail for two reasons: the file is missing (the kvm module is not loaded or the processor has no virtualization extensions; error ENOENT) or the permissions do not allow it (EACCES). Write a function kvm_access(ls_line, user, groups): ls_line is the line printed by ls -l /dev/kvm (or an empty string if the file is missing), user is the user name, groups is the list of the user's group names (including the primary one). Return "ENOENT" if the file is missing; otherwise "ok" or "EACCES". Opening for reading and writing needs both the r and w bits. Take the set of permissions that applies to the user: first the owner (if the name equals the owner), else the group (if the file's group is in groups), else others. The user root always passes. The permission string may be longer than ten characters: it can end with + (ACL) or . (SELinux context); ignore them. ACLs are not interpreted here.
tasks.hint: split() gives the fields: [0] permissions, [2] owner, [3] group. The permissions are the first 10 characters; characters 1-3 are the owner, 4-6 the group, 7-9 others.

tasks.title: Three descriptor levels from strace
tasks.statement: strace shows how a VMM talks to KVM: strace can print ioctl names from linux/kvm.h. A descriptor from open("/dev/kvm") is a system one, from KVM_CREATE_VM a VM descriptor, from KVM_CREATE_VCPU a vCPU one. Write a function fd_levels(lines): lines are strace lines (for example, openat(AT_FDCWD, "/dev/kvm", O_RDWR|O_CLOEXEC) = 3, ioctl(3, KVM_CREATE_VM, 0) = 4, close(4) = 0). Return a list of tuples (descriptor number, "system" | "vm" | "vcpu"), sorted by number, for the descriptors still open at the end of the log. Rules: calls with a negative result (= -1 ENOMEM (...)) create nothing; open/openat count only if the path is "/dev/kvm"; KVM_CREATE_VM creates a VM only if issued on a system descriptor; KVM_CREATE_VCPU creates a vCPU only if issued on a VM descriptor; close(N) removes the descriptor (the number may be reused later); skip all other lines. If strace runs with -f, lines may start with [pid  411]: drop that prefix (the descriptor table is shared).
tasks.hint: A regular expression like name(args) = number. For ioctl the first argument is the descriptor number and the second is the request name.
